COMPUTATIONAL VISUAL PERCEPTION
Mooney Faces
Project Part 1 · individual project · 100 photographs and their binary transformations

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
01
What survives
when shading
becomes binary?
Hadis Nouri
Depth Anything V2 Small + CLIP ViT-B/32
100 originals · 100 Mooneys · 2 vision systems
Original
Mooney
Example 010 · source FFHQ 00041 · 1024 × 1024

APPROACH / ALL THREE TASKS
Faces under a controlled loss of shading
Question: do category preference, depth structure, and same-photo matching survive the Mooney transformation?

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
02


01  Choose the images
100 aligned FFHQ photographs, each supplied at 1024 × 1024.

512 candidates screened; 150 pairs visually reviewed by the assistant for facial structure and background clutter.

No model predictions used for selection.


02  Make the Mooneys
Grayscale → Gaussian blur → global brightness threshold.

Sigma 8 px; kernel 49 px. White-pixel target 22% or 28%, recorded per image.

Student viewed the review board and selected the final ten pairs.


03  Test two systems
Depth Anything V2 Small: relative inverse-depth consistency.

CLIP ViT-B/32: prompt-relative face preference and embedding matching.

Both systems process all 100 originals and all 100 Mooneys.

TASK 2 / ACTUAL RUNNING TOOL
Interactive controls, shared with the batch generator
Screenshot captured from the local GUI. Moving the sliders changes the actual full-resolution PNG.

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
03
Two independent controls
White-pixel percentage
Controls the proportion that remains white.

Blur sigma (pixels)
Controls smoothing before thresholding.

Batch CLI
Single images, folders, per-image CSV.
Verified: 101-image batch + nine parameter combinations + browser interaction.

TASK 2 / IMPLEMENTATION
A reproducible Mooney transformation
Actual source screenshot; the complete editable source is provided in the repository and source archive.

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
04
1  Grayscale in float32

2  Gaussian smoothing
    k = 2 × ceil(3 × sigma) + 1

3  Global brightness threshold
    requested white count = floor(N × p / 100)

4  Deterministic boundary ties
    tie handling is recorded in the CSV
Generation preserves input dimensions. No image generator, edge tracing, or segmentation is used.

TASK 2 / CONTROL DEMONSTRATION
Blur and white percentage change different properties
One source photograph (010) is held fixed. Nine binary results are generated by the same function.

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
05
Fixed original: image 010
Rows: 16%, 28%, 40% white
Columns: sigma 0, 8, 16 px

Final settings are logged separately for every image.

TASK 2 / STUDENT-SELECTED SUBSET
The ten manually selected pairs
Hadis Nouri viewed the review board and explicitly confirmed these ten IDs. Each pair: original on the left, Mooney on the right.

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
06

The Subset files are byte-identical copies of the corresponding full-set files.

TASK 3 / SYSTEM DECLARATION
Two pretrained vision systems, no project-specific training
One-person team: the brief requires two systems. All 200 input images are processed by each system.

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
07


01  Depth Anything V2 Small
Task: monocular relative inverse depth.

Official model: depth-anything/Depth-Anything-V2-Small-hf

Default processor; output bicubically interpolated to 1024 × 1024. Export: 16-bit normalized depth + INFERNO visualization.


02  CLIP ViT-B/32
Task: image/text similarity and visual embeddings.

Official model: openai/clip-vit-base-patch32

Eight fixed prompts; face score sums the two face-prompt shares. Visual embeddings are unit-normalized for matching.
Official checkpoint hashes and model/config revisions are verified and stored in run_info.json.

SYSTEM 1 / QUALITATIVE RESULTS
Depth structure is partly preserved, with visible failures
Examples at the 10th, 50th, and 90th positions of the sorted paired correlations; no best-only selection.

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
08
Mean paired correlation
0.484
Each depth visualization is independently normalized. Brighter INFERNO colors indicate higher relative inverse depth within that image.

Color similarity across images does not establish metric depth.

SYSTEM 1 / QUANTITATIVE RESULTS
Corresponding pairs exceed an unrelated-image control
Full-resolution pixel-wise Pearson correlation: original depth vs. Mooney depth; control pairs original i with Mooney i+1 (cyclic).

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
09
Paired mean 0.484     |     control mean 0.284     |     79/100 paired maps above control

SYSTEM 2 / CATEGORY PREFERENCE
CLIP retains a strong face-prompt preference
The eight-prompt comparison is fixed for originals and Mooneys. These scores are relative softmax shares, not calibrated probabilities.

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
10
Mean face-prompt share: originals 0.836; Mooneys 0.913.

SYSTEM 2 / INDIVIDUAL OUTPUTS
Examples include the Mooney face-prompt failure
Three subset examples plus the image whose top Mooney prompt is not a face. All eight prompt scores are saved per image.

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
11

TWO SYSTEMS / OPTIONAL MATCHING ANALYSIS
Same-photo matching survives above the 12.5% baseline
One correct gallery image + seven distinct distractors; shuffled positions, seed 0; identical gallery design for both systems and directions.

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
12
What is being matched?
Original and Mooney views of the same photograph.

CLIP: cosine similarity of 512-D image embeddings.

Depth: correlation of maps resized to 64 × 64, centered and unit-normalized.

Error bars: Wilson 95% intervals.

INTERPRETATION / RELATION TO THE PAPERS
Recognizing a face and recovering identity are different
Category preference is high, while matching the corresponding photograph remains substantially harder.

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
13


Paper 1: inspiration
Egger et al. compare inverse rendering with feedforward accounts on atypical faces.

This project uses their Mooney motivation and a related eight-alternative matching format.

Our same-photo test does not reproduce their cross-pose identity experiment or human comparison.


Limits of the current evidence
No true depth is available: depth-map agreement measures consistency.

The face-prompt share depends on the prompt set; it is not recognition accuracy across object categories.

Paper 2 studies fly visual motion circuits and informs later project parts; FlyVis is not one of these two systems.

DELIVERY / REPRODUCIBILITY
The submission follows the required folder structure
Source code, provenance, parameters, embeddings and analysis tables are provided separately for reproducibility.

DECLARATION / AI USAGE
AI assistance is disclosed explicitly
The photographs are sourced from FFHQ. Their source credits and individual licenses are listed in the following appendix.

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
15
ChatGPT / Codex assisted with:
Reading the supplied brief and papers; writing and reviewing code; screening source images and choosing transformation settings; executing models; computing statistics; preparing figures, presentation and submission checks.

Student decision and computed evidence
Hadis Nouri reviewed the proposed subset board and selected the ten final pairs. Model outputs and numerical results were computed by the supplied programs. No generative-image model or invented human 1–5 ratings were used.

SOURCES / METHODS AND MODELS
References and reproducibility records

HADIS NOURI  /  COMPVP  /  PART 1
16
Project brief
CompVP Project Part 1, supplied lecture slides, 26 October 2026. Tasks 1–3 and submission requirements.
Paper 1
Egger, Siegel, Arora, Soltani & Yildirim. Inverse Rendering Best Explains Face Perception Under Extreme Illuminations. Supplied PDF.
Paper 2
Lappalainen et al. Connectome-constrained networks predict neural activity across the fly visual system. Nature (2024).
Image collection
FFHQ (NVlabs). Aligned photographs from pinned mirror revision 505f94e2ecc6db64e967e8e6c8e2c2079ea0876b. Individual photo credits follow.
Depth model
Depth Anything V2 Small. Official checkpoint revision 5426e4f0f36572d16453bbda7a8389317b1bef99.
CLIP model
CLIP ViT-B/32. Official config revision 3d74acf9a28c67741b2f4f2ea7635f0aaf6f0268; verified weights and environment in run_info.json.
